items.text: The First Route Sells The First Route Sells The first route sells a skill you can repeat for many farms, so it leads. The business routes follow, because each has a real customer and something you can own.

rows: CUET (ICAR-UG) merit rank, then ICAR counselling. The bulletin says the exam covers 20 percent of university seats, and 100 percent at six named institutions. There is no direct nomination without the exam.

Class 12 needs at least three of Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Biology and Agriculture, with 50 percent marks (40 percent for SC, ST and PwBD). Many universities add an age cap, such as 22 years at one and 25 years at another.
State quota seat at a state agricultural university
The university or state runs its own admission process for the remaining seats. Rules and subject lists differ by state.
Ask the university for last year's cut-off and fee. We found no reliable national fee table, so we print none.
Private college affiliated to a university
Admission follows the college and its university. ICAR accreditation is a separate step that ICAR gives to colleges.
Check the college on the current ICAR list before you pay. Student Q&A pages say employers weigh ICAR status differently, so read the notice for each post you want.

items.heading: Shortlist Two Routes
items.text: Shortlist two routes. Use the routes table and the four questions. Park the other ten for now.

items.heading: Do One Small Piece
items.text: Do one small piece of work in each. Write a crop plan for a relative's plot, spend time behind an input shop counter, or sit in on an FPO meeting. Take the time your life allows.

items.heading: Talk to People Who Did
items.text: Talk to people who did it. Find two people who stayed in each route and one who left. Ask how they found their first paying farmer or employer.

items.heading: Write Down the Route
items.text: Write down the route you drop. If you cannot choose what to drop, you are still comparing job titles.

figures.source: The national mission on natural farming was approved on 25 November 2024 with a Rs 2,481 crore outlay, 15,000 clusters and a goal of 1 crore farmers. The plan includes 10,000 input resource centres and a simpler certification with a common brand.
